texts.preamble: Farukh And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 23 July, 2019 Bench: Shashi Kant Gupta, Saurabh Shyam Shamshery High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Court No. - 32 Case :- Writ - C No. - 23802 of 2019 Petitioner :- Farukh And Another Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others
texts.facts: This writ petition has been filed, inter alia, for the following reliefs :- "i) Issue a writ order or direction into the nature of mandamus directing the respondent authorities that they will not interfere into the peaceful running of shop nos.796 & shop no.56 of the petitioners, situated at Main Bazar, near Bus Stand, Bahadurgarh, Garhmukeshwar, District Hapur. ii) Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the respondent No. 2 that he will decide the representation dated 02.07.2019 made by the petitioners." Farukh And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 23 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97059110/ 1 Petitioners' claim to have individual certificate of Registration under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred as to 'the Act of 2006') for conducting business of retail meat shop (meat and meat products including poultry) which is valid up to 09.08.2024.
texts.arguments: Shri Awadhesh Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that petitioners have valid registration for retail meat shop (meat and meat products including poultry) but the respondents - District Administration and District Food and Safety Officer are unnecessary forcing the petitioners to stop their business. Learned counsel for the petitioners further submitted that the respondents have illegally stopped their vehicle which was used for transporting the meat as well as threaten the petitioners to stop their business. The act of the respondent is infringing the petitioners' right to run their business as provided under Article 19 of the Constitution of India. Learned counsel for the petitioners has also relied upon the judgment passed by the Apex Court in the case of State Of Gujarat vs Mirzapur Moti Kureshi Kassab reported at 2005 8 SCC 535, as well as the judgment passed by the Division Bench of this Court in the matter of Mohd. Mustafa & others vs. Union of India Thru. Secretary Ministry Health & Family Welfare in order to show that the petitioners' right of food business cannot be disturbed without due process of law. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents submitted that the petitioners have approached the District Magistrate, Hapur by submitting an application dated 02.07.2019 wherein they have mentioned that the District Administration is not permitting them to slaughter at their shop as well as petitioners may be permitted to carry the meat from the slaughter houses situated at Rampur, Ghaziabad and Meerut even in a vehicle which is an non-air conditional vehicle. It is further submitted that the registration/license for food business are provided under Chapter 2 of the Food Safety and Standards (licensing and registration of food business) Regulations, 2011. Schedule 4 part 1 of (Regulation No. 2.1.1(2)) provide measures to be adopted by the such registration holder. One of the condition is to keep the food in hygienic manner. No permission has been granted to the petitioner for slaughtering. Learned counsel further submits that the petitioners have to follow Regulations prescribed under the Regulations 2011 as well as notification issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) time to time. Considered the submissions made by the rival parties and perused the records. For reference, relevant part of the Regulations (Schedule 4 part 1) is quoted hereinafter :- "SANITARY AND HYGIENIC REQUIREMENTS FOR FOOD MANUFACTURER/ PROCESSOR/HANDLER The place where food is manufactured, processed or handled shall comply with the following requirements: 1. The premises shall be located in a sanitary place and free from filthy surroundings and shall maintain overall hygienic environment. Both the said requests are contrary to the conditions of Registration and Regulations as mentioned above as well as judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Laxmi Narain Modi v. Union of India reported at (2014) 2 SCC 417 wherein certain directions have been passed to modernize the slaughter houses.
